title: Block Algebra: Structure, Factoring, and Fluency
description: A guided and game-based lesson that uses algebra tiles, explanation, and symbolic transfer tasks to develop evidence about polynomial structure, factoring, and completing the square.

audience.description: Secondary learners beginning or reviewing polynomial factoring with area models.

objectives.name: Represent polynomial structure concretely
objectives.description: Represent a polynomial as the corresponding counts of x-squared, x, and unit area tiles.

objectives.name: Factor polynomials with an area model
objectives.description: Arrange algebra tiles into a solid rectangle and connect its dimensions to a polynomial factorization.

objectives.name: Distinguish unlike algebraic terms
objectives.description: Explain why unit, x, and x-squared terms represent unlike quantities and cannot be substituted for one another.

objectives.name: Complete the square with an area model
objectives.description: Determine the constant needed to complete a perfect-square trinomial and explain the geometric relationship.

accessibility.fallback: Use the assistant-led symbolic and verbal area-model activity when pointer controls are not accessible.
Use untimed assistant-presented factorization targets and explain the required tiles and rectangle dimensions.

criteria.description: Completes levels 1 through 3 with accurate tile counts.
Completes deliberate rectangle-building targets across distinct polynomials.
Determines and places the correct number of units to complete the square.
Uses constructed, non-chain clears across multiple targets.
Interprets speed only after accounting for practice, controls, stress, and board conditions.
Explains how rectangle dimensions, tile types, and polynomial factors correspond.
Factors or completes square problems without relying on the game geometry.
evidenceDescriptors: Transfer across at least two non-identical items

criteria.description: Identifies a useful strategy and a remaining uncertainty.

activities.title: Orient and predict
activities.description: Establish prior experience and connect polynomial terms to tile types.

instructions.student: Describe what the x-squared, x, and unit tiles would represent in x² + 3x + 2.
instructions.assistant: Ask for a prediction before teaching. Record the response as diagnostic evidence, including any help provided.
instructions.teacher: Invite learners to compare representations without correcting every detail before the walkthrough.

activities.title: Guided Block Algebra walkthrough
activities.description: Complete the deliberate build, factor, complete-square, and advanced targets.

instructions.student: Complete the walkthrough through at least level 7. Attempt level 8 and continue through levels 9–10 if ready.
instructions.assistant: Launch the game. After claiming the result, interpret deliberate check attempts and failure reasons. Do not convert the pilot bands directly into mastery.
instructions.teacher: Mechanical overlap failures and resets are not algebra errors. Use the learner's explanations to clarify ambiguous attempts.

activities.title: Explain the rectangle
activities.description: Use a short adaptive conversation to test the reasoning behind the game performance.

instructions.student: Explain how the rectangle's dimensions tell you the factors. Be ready for a new example.
instructions.assistant: Choose prompts dynamically from the learner's walkthrough evidence. Ask a dimension prediction, misconception check, or complete-square explanation rather than reciting a fixed answer key.
instructions.teacher: You may contribute an attributed observation, but distinguish prompting from independent learner reasoning.

activities.title: Block Algebra Drop practice
activities.description: Become familiar with the arcade controls without using this round for proficiency claims.

instructions.student: Play one practice game to learn the controls. This round is just for getting comfortable and will not count against you.
instructions.assistant: Treat the result as activity completion and control-familiarity context, not proficiency evidence.
instructions.teacher: Offer an untimed alternative if pointer control or arcade pressure is a barrier.

activities.title: Block Algebra Drop fluency round
activities.description: Complete a qualifying round for fluency evidence after learning the controls.

instructions.student: Play for at least six minutes or until at least ten targets have been offered. You may request the untimed alternative.
instructions.assistant: Use constructed clears only. Treat time-to-clear as secondary and attach stress, dexterity, duration, and target-count caveats.
instructions.teacher: Do not use a single weak arcade session as negative evidence of algebra understanding.

activities.title: Transfer beyond the tiles
activities.description: Solve and explain ordinary symbolic problems without relying on the game geometry.

instructions.student: Factor two non-identical quadratic expressions and explain one result. If complete-square work was attempted, also explain how to choose the missing constant in x² + bx + ?.
instructions.assistant: Generate fresh items appropriate to the demonstrated level. Assess accuracy, reasoning, independence, and transfer. Keep tutoring assistance separate from the final independent attempt.
instructions.teacher: Accept writing, an image of handwritten work, or an attributed live observation.

activities.title: Reflect and create the report
activities.description: Record a learner reflection and generate a lesson-specific report.

instructions.student: Name one strategy that helped and one idea you would like to practice next.
instructions.assistant: Record the reflection as self-report evidence, never as mastery by itself. Generate the report with evidence references, assistance, caveats, and next steps.
instructions.teacher: Review the report's cited evidence rather than relying only on its headline level.
